extracted.intended_audience: requirements engineers, legal experts, and researchers/practitioners developing automated GDPR compliance checking for data processing agreements (DPAs)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and operationalizing GDPR-derived compliance requirements for Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) and building automated (SR/SF/NLP-based) methods to check DPAs against those requirements; includes methodology steps, evaluation practices, and a list of explicit 'shall' requirements drawn from GDPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: R27 (MD7) Organizational and technical measures (Art. 32(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The organizational and technical measures to ensure a level of security can include: (a) pseudonymization and encryption of personal data, (b) ensure confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems and services, (c) restore the availability and access to personal data in a timely manner in the event of a physical or technical incident, and (d) regularly testing, assessing and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organizational measures for ensuring the security of the processing. (Art. 32(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of example measures provided by GDPR; treat these as optional DPA compliance requirements to check for presence/commitments in DPA text.

rubrics_metrics.name: R28 (MD8) Personal data breach notification content (Art. 33(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The notification of personal data breach shall at least include (a) the nature of personal data breach; (b) the name and contact details of the data protection officer; (c) the consequences of the breach; (d) the measures taken or proposed to mitigate its effects. (Art. 33(3))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that DPA breach-notification clauses include these explicit elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: R29 (MD9) DPIA minimum content (Art. 35(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: The DPIA shall at least include (a) a systematic description of the envisaged processing operations and the purposes of the processing, (b) an assessment of the necessity and proportionality of the processing operations in relation to the purposes, (c) an assessment of the risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, and (d) the measures envisaged to address the risks. (Art. 35(7))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check DPAs for commitments to DPIA content or references to DPIA requirements aligned to these four items.

rubrics_metrics.name: R30 (PO20) Processor transfers restriction (Art. 28(3)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The processor shall not transfer personal data to a third country or international organization without a prior specific or general authorization of the controller. (Art. 28(3)(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect and flag DPA provisions permitting or forbidding cross-border transfers absent controller authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: R31 (PO21) Processor guarantees via codes/certification (Art. 28(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The processor can demonstrate guarantees to Article 28 (1–4) through adherence to an approved codes of conduct or an approved certification mechanism. (Art. 28(5))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify whether DPAs reference such codes of conduct or certification as evidence of guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: R32 (PO22) Processor security measures proportional to risk (Art. 32(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The processor shall implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk of varying likelihood and severity for the rights and freedoms of natural persons. (Art. 32(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether DPA commits processor to measures scaled to risk; detect vague or missing commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: R33 (PO23) Processor personnel processing on controller instructions (Art. 32(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The processor shall ensure that any natural person acting under its authority who has access to personal data only process them on instructions from the controller. (Art. 32(4))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for clauses that limit processor personnel to act only per controller instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: R34 (PO24) Processor breach notification to controller (Art. 33(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The processor shall notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach. (Art. 33(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm DPA contains prompt-notification obligation and any timing/window details (e.g., 'without undue delay').

rubrics_metrics.name: R35 (PO25) Processor liability (Art. 82(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A processor shall be liable for the damage caused by processing only where it has not complied with GDPR obligations specifically directed to processors or where it has acted outside or contrary to lawful instructions of the controller. (Art. 82(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect allocation of liability clauses consistent with GDPR (liability limited to processor-specific obligations/non-instruction compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: R36 (CO1) Controller notification to supervisory authority within 72 hours (Art. 33(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The controller shall inform the supervisory authority no later than 72 hours after having become aware of a personal data breach. (Art. 33(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether DPA allocates responsibilities or cooperation for meeting the 72-hour supervisory authority notification requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: R37 (CO2) Controller documentation of personal data breaches (Art. 33(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The controller shall document personal data breaches. (Art. 33(5))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify DPA commitments for breach-recordkeeping and what each party must document.

rubrics_metrics.name: R38 (CO3) Communication to data subjects in case of high risks (Art. 34(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of high risks, the controller shall communicate the data breach to the data subject without undue delay. (Art. 34(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect whether DPAs define responsibilities for controller/processor cooperation when communication to data subjects is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: R39 (CO4) Controller shall carry out a DPIA (Art. 35(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The controller shall carry out a DPIA. (Art. 35(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check DPAs for references/commitments to performing DPIAs where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: R40 (CO5) Controller shall seek advice of the DPO when carrying a DPIA (Art. 35(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The controller shall seek advice of the DPO when carrying a DPIA. (Art. 35(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify clauses which require controller to consult DPO and specify roles/cooperation in DPIAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: R41 (CO6) Controller shall seek views of data subjects on intended processing (Art. 35(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: The controller shall seek the views of data subjects or their representatives on the intended processing. (Art. 35(9))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether DPA references consultation obligations and how responsibility is allocated.

rubrics_metrics.name: R42 (CO7) Controller review when there is a change of risk (Art. 35(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: The controller shall carry out a review to assess if processing is performed in accordance with the data protection impact assessment at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations. (Art. 35(11))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect DPA clauses about periodic review/update obligations tied to changing risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: R43 (CO8) Controller liability for GDPR-infringing processing (Art. 82(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A controller shall be liable for the damage caused by any processing infringing the GDPR. (Art. 82(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify DPAs do not attempt to disclaim controller liability inconsistent with GDPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: R44 (CR2) Controller right to suspend processing (Linklaters LLP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The controller shall have the right to suspend the processing in certain cases. (Linklaters LLP)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check DPA for explicit controller rights to suspend processing and defined trigger conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: R45 (CR3) Controller right to terminate the DPA (Linklaters LLP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The controller shall have the right to terminate the DPA in certain cases. (Linklaters LLP)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect termination rights and the circumstances under which controller may terminate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'shall' requirements as canonical requirement format
rubrics_metrics.description: Define DPA-related compliance requirements as 'shall' requirements; motivated by familiarity of requirements engineers and legal experts with this format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extracting and documenting requirements from GDPR, phrase obligations as 'shall' statements to improve clarity and alignment with legal drafting and RE templates (e.g., Rupp's, EARS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define semantic frames (SFs) over compliance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Define semantic frames (SFs) over the compliance requirements derived from the regulation (G) with respect to a document type (T).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify whether existing semantic roles (SRs) can be re-used; if not, refine SRs in collaboration with legal experts. This step is lightweight (~10% effort per the authors' estimate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use semantic roles / semantic metadata (SRs) to represent legal concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use SRs (semantic metadata) to characterize DPA-related information content (e.g., actor, sanction) and to facilitate transforming legal text to formal specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRs are a prerequisite for deriving compliance requirements and enable phrasal-level automated checking; adapt SRs from literature or define domain-specific ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume conformance with a predefined DPA template
rubrics_metrics.description: Automation should be applicable to any DPA and does not assume conformance with any predefined template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design matching/threshold strategies and SR extraction to work across heterogeneous DPA language and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements elicitation from regulation G with respect to document type T
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements elicitation from G with respect to T, consuming about 30% of the effort. This step depends mainly on the availability of legal experts and the size and complexity of the provisions in G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform elicitation in close collaboration with legal experts; prioritize based on provision complexity and expert availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curate annotated dataset for document type T
rubrics_metrics.description: Curate an annotated dataset for T, consuming about 10% of the effort. Curating a labeled dataset of examples from T is a prerequisite for developing any automation. The annotation task involves manually checking the compliance of the textual content of T against the requirements derived from G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure availability of unlabeled data, recruit annotators with right expertise, provide training material about compliance with respect to G, and document annotation guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop an automation strategy for checking T against G
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop an automation strategy for checking the compliance of T against G, consuming about 50% of the effort. Main adjustments include extraction rules of SRs and similarity thresholds for matching predicates and arguments between the text of T and requirements of G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iteratively tune extraction rules and similarity thresholds; consider hybrid rule-based and ML approaches; focus automation effort on the most variable and semantically challenging components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation design: dataset curation and annotator practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigate bias by curating evaluation datasets exclusively through third-parties (non-authors), ensure annotators are never exposed to implementation details, and involve legal experts for requirement extraction to reduce subjectivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make extracted requirements publicly available for scrutiny; use trained third-party annotators with legal backgrounds; blind annotators to system implementation to reduce internal validity threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics to report for automated compliance checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Report standard classification/assessment metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall; example results reported: average accuracy 84.6%, precision 89.1%, recall 82.4%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precision/recall/accuracy and consider targeted/focused manual review on a small percentage of statements to further improve effective accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider word-sense disambiguation quality when enriching texts
rubrics_metrics.description: The approach relies on most-frequent sense (MFS) disambiguation for identifying semantically related words to enrich DPA texts; this reliance is a potential threat to internal validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider using more advanced WSD/disambiguation methods where appropriate, as they may improve matching and detection accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focused manual review to boost overall accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher accuracy can be achieved by focused reviews on a small percentage of DPA statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use automated detection to prioritize statements for manual review (active learning / human-in-the-loop) to gain accuracy improvements with limited human effort.
